gapFill.title: Fill in the gaps
gapFill.subtitle: Type the correct form of the verb in brackets. Check each clause’s time separately: past condition + present result, or present condition + past result. Twenty original sentences.

questions.before: If I
questions.after: to bed earlier, I wouldn’t be so tired now.
questions.explain: The bedtime was last night (past): had + gone.

questions.before: If I had gone to bed earlier, I
questions.explain: ‘Now’ shows a present result: wouldn’t + base verb.

questions.before: If she hadn’t missed the plane, she
questions.explain: ‘Today’ is now: would + be.

questions.before: If we
questions.after: that flat, we’d live by the sea now.
questions.explain: Buying was in the past: had + bought.

questions.before: If he had studied medicine, he
questions.explain: A present result of a past decision: would be.

questions.before: If I
questions.after: my leg last month, I’d play in the final tomorrow.
questions.explain: ‘Last month’ is past: hadn’t + broken.

questions.before: If you had listened to me, we
questions.explain: ‘Now’ → present result: wouldn’t be.

questions.before: If they had saved money, they
questions.explain: A present result (today): would + have (the verb ‘have’, not a past form).

questions.before: If I had learnt to drive, I
questions.explain: Present ability as a result: could + base verb.

questions.before: If it
questions.after: all night, the pitch would be dry now.
questions.explain: The rain was last night: hadn’t + rained.

questions.before: If I
questions.after: more organised, I wouldn’t have forgotten your birthday.
questions.explain: Being disorganised is a permanent present fact: ‘were’.

questions.before: If I were more organised, I
questions.explain: The forgetting was in the past: wouldn’t have + forgotten.

questions.before: If he
questions.after: so far away, he would have come to the party.
questions.explain: Where he lives is a present fact: didn’t + live.

questions.before: If she spoke better English, she
questions.explain: The interview was in the past: would have + passed.

questions.before: If I
questions.after: afraid of flying, I’d have gone to Japan last summer.
questions.explain: The fear is permanent (present): weren’t.

questions.before: If you weren’t so shy, you
questions.explain: A possible past result: might have + made.

questions.before: If my brother
questions.after: how to cook, he would have made dinner yesterday.
questions.explain: He can’t cook in general (present): past simple ‘knew’.

questions.before: If we had a car, we
questions.explain: The wedding was in the past: would have + driven.

questions.before: If I
questions.after: horror films, I would have gone with you last night.
questions.explain: Your taste is a present fact: past simple ‘liked’.

questions.before: If Anna weren’t so busy, she
questions.explain: Saturday is past: would have + helped.

timedMC.title: Beat the clock
timedMC.subtitle: 15 seconds per question. Check the time of each clause separately — look for now, today, yesterday and permanent facts.

questions.text: If I had slept more last night, I        so tired now.
wrongReasons: ‘Now’ shows a present result, so not ‘wouldn’t have been’.
questions.explain: The sleep was last night (past), but the tiredness is now: wouldn’t + base verb.

questions.text: If she        the job last year, she’d be living in London now.
wrongReasons: ‘Accepted’ is second conditional; ‘last year’ needs the past perfect.
questions.explain: ‘Last year’ puts the condition in the past: had + past participle, ‘had accepted’.

questions.text: If we hadn’t missed the bus, we        at home now.
wrongReasons: ‘Would have been’ is past; ‘now’ needs the present.
questions.explain: The bus was missed in the past, but ‘now’ makes the result present: would be.

questions.text: If he had studied harder at school, he        a better job today.
wrongReasons: ‘Would have had’ is past; ‘today’ is present.
questions.explain: ‘Today’ is a present result of past studying: would + have (here ‘have’ means possess).

questions.text: If I        my phone at home, I could call you now.
wrongReasons: ‘Didn’t leave’ is second conditional; leaving it was in the past.
questions.explain: Leaving the phone happened earlier (past), so the if-clause takes ‘hadn’t left’.

questions.text: If I        more organised, I wouldn’t have missed the deadline.
wrongReasons: ‘Had been’ is possible but means only that time; a character trait is present.
questions.explain: Being disorganised is a permanent quality (present), so the if-clause takes ‘were’.

questions.text: If he didn’t live so far away, he        to my party last week.
questions.explain: Where he lives is present, but the party was last week: would have + past participle.

questions.text: If she        Italian, she would have understood the film.
wrongReasons: ‘Had spoken’ suggests a past moment; speaking a language is a present ability.
questions.explain: Speaking a language is a present ability, so the if-clause uses the past simple ‘spoke’.

questions.text: If I weren’t allergic to cats, I        the kitten.
wrongReasons: The kitten was offered in the past, so ‘would take’ doesn’t fit here.
‘Took’ is a fact, not a result.
questions.explain: The allergy is permanent (present), but the kitten was offered in the past: would have taken.

questions.text: If you        so shy, you might have won the talent show.
wrongReasons: Shyness is a permanent trait, so the present form is better.
questions.explain: Shyness is a general, present trait, so the if-clause uses ‘weren’t’, not ‘hadn’t been’.

questions.text: If I had won the lottery, I        in a mansion now.
wrongReasons: ‘Would have lived’ is past; ‘now’ is present.
questions.explain: Winning would have been in the past, but living in a mansion is ‘now’: would live.

questions.text: If I had won the lottery, I        a house last year.
questions.explain: Both the win and the purchase are in the past (‘last year’): a pure third conditional.

questions.text: If I had a car, I        you to the airport tomorrow.
wrongReasons: ‘Would have driven’ is past; ‘tomorrow’ is future.
questions.explain: Not having a car is now and the drive is tomorrow: a pure second conditional.

questions.text: If I had a car, I        you to the airport yesterday.
questions.explain: Not having a car is a present fact, but the trip was yesterday: would have driven.

questions.text: If you had told me the truth, I        angry now.
questions.explain: The lie was in the past, but the anger is ‘now’: wouldn’t + base verb.

questions.text: If they had planted trees ten years ago, the park        shady now.
wrongReasons: ‘Would have been’ is past; ‘now’ is present.
questions.explain: Present result: would be.

questions.text: If my dad        to music, he would have come to the concert.
wrongReasons: A general habit is present, so the past simple is better.
questions.explain: Not listening to music is his general habit (present), so use the past simple ‘listened’.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?
choices: If I would have studied, I’d be a doctor now.
If I had studied, I’d be a doctor now.
If I had studied, I’d have been a doctor now.
If I studied, I’d have been a doctor now.
wrongReasons: Studying was in the past: ‘had studied’.
questions.explain: Studying was in the past (had studied) and being a doctor is now (would be).

questions.text: If I        how to swim, I would have joined you in the lake.
wrongReasons: Not knowing how to swim is a present fact.
questions.explain: Not knowing how to swim is a present fact, so the if-clause uses the past simple ‘knew’.

questions.text: If I hadn’t eaten that sandwich, I        sick now.
questions.explain: Eating the sandwich was in the past, but feeling sick is now: wouldn’t + feel.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong (if a word is missing, tap the word right after the gap). Twenty original sentences.

items.message: ‘Now’ → present result: wouldn’t + base verb, ‘wouldn’t feel’.
Present result: after ‘would’ use the base verb, ‘would have a car’.
Present result: ‘we would be home now’ — after ‘would’ use ‘be’.
‘Last month’ is past: ‘If I hadn’t broken my leg…’.
After ‘would have’ use the participle: broken.
Imaginary present result: ‘we would have a table’.
Imaginary past result: ‘I would have got the job’.
Last night is past: ‘If it hadn’t rained…’.
An imaginary present: ‘If I were braver…’.
Past perfect: ‘If they had left earlier…’.

levelCheck.title: How well do you know it?
levelCheck.subtitle: 20 mixed questions — typing, word order, timelines, multiple choice and spot-the-mistake. In the typing questions check the time of each clause before you write. One pass, then a breakdown of where you’re strong and where to go back and practise.

items.sentText: If I {{blank}} a jacket, I wouldn’t be cold now.
items.explain: Forgetting the jacket was in the past: had + brought.

items.sentText: If she had trained harder, she {{blank}} in the team now.
If I {{blank}} good at maths, I would have helped you with the test.
If he weren’t so lazy, he {{blank}} yesterday.

items.text: I didn’t study medicine. I’m not a doctor. → If I {{blank}} medicine, I’d be a doctor.
wrongReasons: ‘Studied’ makes the condition present, but studying was in the past.

items.text: I’m afraid of dogs, so I didn’t go to her house. → If I weren’t afraid of dogs, I {{blank}} to her house.
wrongReasons: ‘Would go’ is present; the visit was in the past.

items.text: Which sentence has a past condition and a present result?
choices: If I’d listened, I’d know now.
If I’d listened, I’d have known.

items.text: Which sentence has a present condition and a past result?
choices: If I’d been taller, I’d be picked.
If I were taller, I’d be picked.
If I were taller, I’d have been picked.
If I’d been taller, I’d have been picked.
wrongReasons: That’s past → present (the other mixed type).
items.explain: were taller (present) + ’d have been picked (past) = mixed.

items.text: If they hadn’t sold the house, they {{blank}} there now.
wrongReasons: ‘Would have lived’ is past; ‘now’ is present.

items.text: If I {{blank}} a better memory, I wouldn’t have forgotten her name.
wrongReasons: A bad memory is a permanent trait: present, so ‘had’ alone.

items.text: If he had taken the medicine, he {{blank}} better today.
If she weren’t so stubborn, she {{blank}} our advice.
wrongReasons: The advice was given in the past.

items.message: Present result: after ‘would’ use ‘be’: ‘I would be fit now’.
